retainedCounterexample.meaning: Successful counterexample and recovery, not successful authority protection. Earlier diagnostic package differs from revised package; do not claim a new revised-package race run.

primarySources.finding: The relation grant path opens pg_class and pg_attribute with RowExclusiveLock and obtains the target pg_class tuple through SearchSysCacheLocked1. These are catalog locks, not the retained AccessShareLock on the protected user relation.
primarySources.evidenceType: Pinned release source inspection; explains retained native counterexample, not new provider observation

primarySources.finding: SELECT admits AccessShareLock; INSERT additionally admits RowExclusiveLock and weaker modes; MAINTAIN, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE admit stronger table modes. Changing a protected-relation lock alone does not address the distinct grant catalog path.
primarySources.evidenceType: Source inference; no new privilege or LOCK command was executed

primarySources.finding: Role alteration uses the shared pg_authid catalog; role grant processing reads pg_authid and modifies pg_auth_members. Protected application/platform table locks do not establish protection for these separate shared authority catalogs.
primarySources.evidenceType: Source inference; no new global-role race execution

primarySources.finding: Database DDL event triggers exclude shared objects such as roles, databases and tablespaces, and changes to event triggers themselves.
primarySources.evidenceType: Official version17 documentation consulted10October; not an immutable17.6 source hash or deployed-provider behavior proof
